Reem's blog

Occasional writing from Reem Glasco, LPC-S, on the things that come up often enough in the room to be worth setting down once: boundaries, what the nervous system is doing, trauma work, and the practical business of being a therapist in Texas.

If you are thinking about therapy

How to Set Healthy Boundaries

Five steps to setting boundaries that hold: identify your limits, say them plainly, read your own feelings, and get help if they keep collapsing.

Read more

Is Equine Therapy Covered by Insurance?

Equine-assisted psychotherapy has no billing code of its own, which is why insurance does not cover it. What to ask your own plan, and what sessions cost here.

Read more

Why Walk and Talk Therapy Works

Walking side by side changes what is possible to say. Why movement and no eye contact help some people talk, and who outdoor therapy does not suit.

Read more

If you are a therapist

What Makes Supervision Trauma-Informed

Trauma-informed supervision treats the supervisee's own nervous system as part of the work. What that changes about case presentation, pacing and shame.

Read more

Start with a conversation

Therapy consults are fifteen minutes. Supervision and EMDR consultation consults are thirty. Both are free and commit you to nothing.

Reem Glasco is a Licensed Professional Counselor Supervisor in Texas, license 66562. Complaints about a Texas licensee go to the Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council, 1-800-821-3205. Nothing on this site is therapy, supervision, or a substitute for either. If you are in immediate danger, call 911. For a mental health crisis, call or text 988 for the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.
